correctness.rationale: Corollary 1.8 reduces the normalizer quotient to the stabilizer of the Artin--Schreier plane. In the first normal form, preservation of the one-dimensional eigenspace forces \(\lambda^2=1\), leaving exactly the Klein four group after adjoining the branch-swap involution. In the second normal form, the exact matrix \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}c&d/r\\rd&c\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) shows that a nontrivial diagonal symmetry beyond \(\lambda=\pm1\) exists exactly when \(r^2\in\mathbf F_p\). On that locus the diagonal stabilizer is the norm-one subgroup of \(\mathbf F_{p^2}^*\), cyclic of order \(p+1\), and the involution acts by inversion, giving a dihedral quotient of order \(2(p+1)\).

value.rationale: The normalizer is an explicit invariant singled out by the source's Corollary 1.8 and Remark 9.4. The calculation completes that invariant across both newly classified two-parameter normal forms, identifies the generic minimum \(4p^2\), and locates a genuine exceptional symmetry stratum where the order jumps to \(2p^2(p+1)\). The norm-one-torus description explains the jump structurally and gives a reusable moduli stratification rather than an arbitrary numerical example.
